about: What the public catalogue page (components.html) says about the story-component shelf, beside what it reads from the engine's doc comments (the first sentence of each part's). One entry per root export whose doc comment carries @shelf, with an example of the same name in src/catalogue/examples; tests/shelfCatalogue.test.ts keeps the three together (O-080 T-335).

jobs.switch: A switch: a button or choice that changes what is shown or where the camera looks
jobs.filter: A filter: lights some of the things in the scene and dims the rest
jobs.readout: A readout: a figure, key or picture that tells the visitor what they are looking at
jobs.explainer: An explainer: words that say what is going on

outOfTheBox.name: Title and About
outOfTheBox.text: The bar shows your title; pressing it opens the About panel with a status line, credits, links and the Built with Astraeus mark (scene.setAbout).

outOfTheBox.name: Picker and views
outOfTheBox.text: A choice in the bar between the things your page offers, and named views of one scene that show some objects and events and not others (scene.setPicker, scene.setViews).

outOfTheBox.name: Display switches
outOfTheBox.text: Orbit lines, labels, the Milky Way and the sky lines, each a button in the bar, a row in one panel or a row in the Developer drawer (scene.setSwitches).

outOfTheBox.name: Timeline
outOfTheBox.text: Play and pause, a speed choice, a scrubber, and a list of the moments you add (scene.setTimeline, scene.addEvents).

outOfTheBox.name: Camera and objects
outOfTheBox.text: An object list, focus and follow, overview and, where you offer it, looking out from a body (scene.camera).

outOfTheBox.name: Info cards
outOfTheBox.text: A card for each body, path or group with its description, readouts, source and known limits.

outOfTheBox.name: Story panels
outOfTheBox.text: Steps or moments with a title and words that can move the camera and select an object (scene.addStoryPanels).

uses.text: Put a story's own button in the bar: it opens a panel that holds the controls for that story.
Give a topic its own place, so the words are one press away and not in the way of the scene.
Draw your own picture or chart in the panel; the engine hands you an empty box and you fill it.
Any control the shelf does not have yet, until it does.
Say what is on screen: a heading, a few paragraphs and a small note for a caveat or a source.
Change the words from your code as the visitor moves the time or the camera.
Buttons that fly the camera to a place the story wants the visitor to see.
A guided tour in a panel: one button for each stop.
Pick one group, or several, to light up while your code dims the rest.
A choice between a few modes of the same scene, shown as chips instead of a menu.
Say what each colour means, with how many things wear it.
Sit beside a set of chips so the visitor can see what each chip lights.
